what_happened: A docs job to correct and complete the firstmate explainer page, citing sources, was rejected. The final verdict was fail because the verifier changed the snapshot it was judging. The system treated that as a blocker because it invalidates the verdict. No acceptance criterion or check is listed as unmet, so the page was not shown to be wrong. The verdict simply cannot be trusted. This is the second time the same job type has ended this way, after 20261015-033445-dtwk.
cause: The verifier still has write access to the snapshot it judges. Nothing makes the snapshot read-only or compares a fingerprint before and after. The only detection is a blocker finding after the verifier has finished, so the whole job is lost. The earlier case did not lead to a fix, so a retry of the same work hit the same failure. The record does not say what the verifier changed or why, so the trigger inside the verifier is unconfirmed.
prevention: Run the verifier against a read-only copy or mount of the snapshot, so writes fail at the filesystem level. Also record a content fingerprint of the snapshot before verification and compare it after. If it differs, discard that verdict and automatically rerun verification on a fresh copy of the snapshot, rather than rejecting the job. Treat a repeated mutation as a system fault to report to the operator, not as a job failure.
proposed_request: Make verification non-mutating. Run the verifier on a read-only copy of the job snapshot. Take a content fingerprint of the snapshot before verification and compare it afterwards. If the fingerprint differs, discard the verdict, rerun verification once on a fresh copy, and flag the job as a system fault instead of rejecting it for the work's quality. Add a test showing that a verifier which tries to write to the snapshot cannot change it, and that a changed fingerprint triggers the rerun. Then rerun the firstmate explainer docs job (correct and complete the page, citing sources) and confirm it reaches a valid verdict.
